t_row_all: Show the log of every app
t_empty: No apps yet. Add each app with its address and read token in the settings.
t_engine: The TollRoll service does not answer. Reinstalling the plugin starts it again.
s_sub: One dashboard tile for your apps: how each one is doing, and one log for all of them.
s_addr_hint: The web address of the app, such as https://192.168.1.10:3443, or the socket of an app that runs as a plugin on this server, such as /var/run/shiplog.sock.
s_token_hint: Create a read token in the app's settings, for example in BombVault, KnightLoader or ArrowLoop. It lets TollRoll read the status and the log and nothing else. It stays on this server and never reaches your browser.
s_found_none: No app on this server answers on a socket.
s_none: No apps yet. Add one with its address and read token, or search this server for apps that run as a plugin.
s_tile_hint: The tile appears on the dashboard by itself. Hide, move or collapse it with Unraid's own tile controls. Click an app or a button above the log to see only that app's lines. The log stays dark on every theme, like a terminal.
e_unauthorized: the app wants a read token
e_not_found: this app does not report its status yet, an update may help
e_bad_answer: the answer is not a status report
e_cert_changed: the app shows a different certificate than before
e_invalid_address: this is not a valid address
e_token_missing: a web address needs a read token
e_duplicate: this address is already in the list
e_too_many: the tile reads at most 32 apps
e_unknown_source: this app was removed in the meantime, reload the page
e_engine: the TollRoll service does not answer
s_notify_hint: While a channel is on, TollRoll checks your apps once a minute. It tells you when an app stops answering, when it answers again and when it shows something new that needs you. Each of these is sent once.
s_n_apprise_hint: The address of a key on your Apprise API server, such as http://192.168.1.10:8000/notify/tollroll.
s_n_err_invalid: a field is missing or not valid
n_down_body: TollRoll could not read {name} for a few minutes. The TollRoll settings show why.
n_test_body: If you read this, TollRoll can reach you here.
